paper_title: Constraining Light QCD Axions with Isolated Neutron Star Cooling
suggested_experiment_name: NS cooling (light QCD axion, this work)
coupling_convention: 1/f_a in GeV^-1, exactly as plotted on the y-axis of Fig. 5 (x-axis is m_a in eV). To obtain f_a [GeV], take the reciprocal; NO conversion was applied.
notes: Paper presents a new astrophysical exclusion of light QCD axions (mass lighter than standard QCD prediction at given f_a) from isolated neutron star cooling. The main result (Fig. 5) is an excluded region in the (m_a [eV], 1/f_a [GeV^-1]) plane, so AxionMass is the correct coupling type; the pre-analysis hint is confirmed. However, no numerical table is given: the exclusion is a 2D band bounded by the epsilon = 0.1 line (right edge, where the new ground state of nuclear matter ceases to exist), a roughly vertical line at low m_a (need for large effective gravity g_a), and diagonals set by NGS formation vs envelope density. The emitted points trace the epsilon = 0.1 right boundary computed from Eq. (13) [(m_a)_vac = sqrt(eps)*m_pi*f_pi*sqrt(beta)/(2 f_a), giving m_a ~ 1.8e-6 eV at f_a = 1e12 GeV] over the f_a range ~1e12-1e17 GeV shown in Figs. 2-4; the full excluded band extends to smaller epsilon (smaller m_a at fixed f_a), roughly down to m_a ~ 1e-12 eV. Values are approximate reconstructions, not digitized from the figure - treat as indicative. No CL is quoted (exclusion criterion is L_gamma(1e5 yr) < 5e30 erg/s, i.e. (g+g_a)_14 > 50-100); 0.95 is a placeholder.
